clauses.reason: Whole order (single operative paragraph, offsets 0-677 of the held text jobs/app-executive-orders/output/texts/executive-order-8524-exemption-j-brent-clarke-from-compulsory-retirement-for-age.txt): signed August 26, 1940. The recital finds that the public interest requires that the employee be exempted from compulsory retirement for age for a period of one year, and the operative sentence, under section 204 of the act of June 30, 1932 (47 Stat. 382, 404), exempts J. Brent Clarke from compulsory retirement for age for a period of one year ending September 30, 1941. That exemption is the order's only command and it carries its own fixed term. First end: the order's own stated end, September 30, 1941 (operative sentence: "for a period of one year ending September 30, 1941."). The stated date is recorded inclusive (the exemption runs through the end of September 30, 1941); the exclusive reading, under which it ends when September 30, 1941 begins, is the alternative. The date is the end of the stated term, not a record of separation or death; no such record is held. Later event, not an end: Executive Order 8866, signed August 22, 1941, further exempts the same person; its recital names this order ("by Executive Order No. 8524 of August 26, 1940") and its operative sentence runs "ending September 30, 1942". Like this order it has no effective-date wording, so I read it as effective on signing. MOMMSEN-I rechecked this stated end against both held witnesses. Own APP has see. 715a where GPO has sec. 715a. This is a disclosed nonmaterial abbreviation typo within the quoted authority parenthetical; section 204, 47 Stat. 382, 404 and the operative exemption/date agree.
